title: At most one defective component in five
scenario_markdown: A quality inspection samples 5 components independently from a manufacturing line with a 10% defect rate ($p=0.10$). Find the probability of observing at most one defective component.

approval.notes: Reviewed derivation for n=5, p=0.1, P(X<=1) = P(X=0)+P(X=1) = 0.59049 + 0.32805 = 0.91854. Verified distractors, 4 stages, and 1-to-1 concept evidence mapping.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which model fits counting defective components in this fixed batch?

options.hint_markdown: Is the number of components fixed in advance, or arriving over continuous time?
Are 0 and 5 defects equally likely when the defect rate is only 10%?

stages.explanation_markdown: The scenario counts successes (defects) across a fixed number $n=5$ of independent trials with identical success probability $p=0.10$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which mathematical expression corresponds to 'at most one defective'?

options.hint_markdown: Does 'at most one' include the value one itself?
Can a batch have zero defects and still satisfy 'at most one'?

stages.explanation_markdown: 'At most one' includes zero and one: $P(X \le 1) = P(X=0) + P(X=1)$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate $P(X \le 1)$. Enter as a decimal or percent rounded to at least three decimal places.
What is the probability of finding two or more defective components?

options.hint_markdown: Probabilities cannot exceed one. How do complementary events partition the sample space?

stages.explanation_markdown: Since $\{X \le 1\}$ and $\{X \ge 2\}$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, $P(X \ge 2) = 1 - P(X \le 1) = 0.08146$.
